newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Acer leads IBM's US$1.73 bln '97 sourcing pact.
newsitem.headline: Acer leads IBM's US$1.73 bln '97 sourcing pact.

text.p: IBM Corp said on Thursday it would buy notebook and desktop computers worth up to US$1.73 billion in 1997 from Taiwan makers, chiefly from local giant Acer Group.
Dang declined to name the other manufacturers.
Acer executives declined to comment on Dang's disclosure.
Dang said the U.S. computer giant did not hesitate to source its computer line in Taiwan and said Acer in particular offered excellent logistical support.
"The reason is simple. Taiwan's computer products are cheap and good," he said.
He noted that IBM was not the biggest buyer of Taiwan computer products, saying it ranked behind Compaq Computer Corp.
